subject.title: fix(cron): keep paced schedules stable across force runs and edits

question: Should this PR preserve equivalent version-1 persisted schedule identities across upgrade, or is recomputing every existing pending cron slot on first reload an accepted compatibility change?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes the durable identity format and scheduler-owned state; only maintainers can accept a potential upgrade-time cadence reset or choose the required migration contract.

options.title: Preserve equivalent legacy identities
options.body: Recommended: treat version-1 identities as equivalent when the schedule is unchanged and neither pacing nor trigger-presence semantics require invalidation, with a rolling-upgrade regression test.

options.title: Accept a documented reset
options.body: Accept recomputation of pending slots for existing stores, but document the upgrade behavior and prove the resulting cadence is safe for recurring, paced, and trigger jobs.

recommendation.title: Preserve equivalent legacy identities
recommendation.body: Recommended: treat version-1 identities as equivalent when the schedule is unchanged and neither pacing nor trigger-presence semantics require invalidation, with a rolling-upgrade regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked report and proposed implementation identify the scheduling-ownership boundary and provide the current repair direction.
